newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli CPI-linked short bonds end sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Israeli CPI-linked short bonds end sharply higher.

text.p: Israeli inflation-linked short bonds rose sharply on Thursday in response to market fears that inflation may accelerate in the second quarter, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): -0.1 pct at 103.09
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.06 pct at 102.38
Volume was moderate at 173 million shekels with most of the trading concentrated in the Makams and unlinked bonds.

"Inflation-linked short bonds rose sharply today after Bank Hapoalim raised its CPI forecast for February to 1.1 percent. Investors feel that inflation might rise sharply in March and April," said a trader at Israel Discount Bank.

"The supply of CPI-linked short bonds is very low and demand is rising because of the inflation fears. The government is expected to issue only long bonds so pressure on the shorts is rising," said Zvi Hoffman of Meitav Investments.
In contrast, unlinked bonds with the exception of Makams suffered losses today because of the change in inflation expectations, the Discount trader said.
"Makams were not affected because they are still attracting private investors," he said, a phenomenon he ascribed to tax considerations.

Traders said dollar-linked bonds were expected to continue rising on Sunday following the sharp decline of the shekel against the U.S. currency. In the local forex market the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3480 shekels against 3.3380 shekels on Wednesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
